A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniAP and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite extensive restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original distributed-training throughput, strategy-search time, scalability and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 4.

after.justification: Section 4 reports original training and optimization results, including additional baseline comparisons, LLaMA experiments and estimation-accuracy analysis. Appendix E also reports FLOPs-utilization comparisons.

M1.justification: The pipeline objective's bottleneck term changes from computation stages alone in v1 Equation 1 to computation and communication stages in v2 Equation 2. This can change strategy selection for communication-dominated pipelines. The joint MIQP framework, supported strategies and UOP enumeration otherwise remain equivalent.

E1.justification: v2 adds causal language modeling with LLaMA-7B and an eight-A100 hardware environment. The original four model workloads and English Wikipedia/ImageNet-1K datasets remain. v1's four-node EnvC becomes v2's EnvD; that scenario is retained.

E2.justification: v1's primary comparisons evaluate Galvatron alone. v2 Table 2 adds Alpa across the retained BERT, T5 and ViT experiments, including reported T5 optimization-memory failures. Alpa is explicitly excluded for Swin and LLaMA. This substantially broadens direct comparison with competing automatic-parallelism systems.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-7B settings with batch size 8, sequence length 2048 and FP16, plus MFU and prediction-error evaluation. Retained experiments keep their batch sizes and throughput averaging over iterations 10–60. Appendix D's blanket FP32 statement conflicts with the LLaMA-specific FP16 description.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained scalability and restricted-strategy studies, v2 Section 4.3 adds direct validation of throughput estimates against measurements and Galvatron. Appendix E extends the existing BERT case study with MFU comparisons. The ablation also revises feasibility outcomes, including changing BERT inter-layer-only execution from successful to infeasible.

E5.justification: v1's main tables provide point estimates; v2 Table 2 adds ± quantities to throughput and optimization-time results. Neither their statistical meaning nor repeat counts and seeds are specified. This establishes changed uncertainty reporting, without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Many existing throughput and optimization-time values are revised, alongside new Alpa, LLaMA, estimation-error and MFU results. For T5-Large-32 on EnvB with batch size 8, UniAP/Galvatron throughput changes from 7.55/4.57 to 7.98/8.06 samples/s, reversing their ranking. v2 additionally reports average estimation errors of 3.59% for UniAP and 11.17% for Galvatron.

T1.justification: v2 revises the timing formulation to maximize over computation and communication costs, dropping v1's assumption that computation stages dominate communication stages. The contiguity definition and Appendix A proof, Appendix B QIP formulation and stated complexity bound otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central novelty claim of jointly optimizing inter- and intra-layer parallelism through MIQP remains. The abstract and introduction update the headline claims from 1.70× throughput and 16× search speedup across four models to 1.71× and 107× across five. The larger optimization-speedup claim concerns the newly added Alpa comparison.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the main-text bandwidth and memory-bound explanation of optimization-time differences with an explanation based on multithreaded MIQP versus single-threaded dynamic programming. It adds interpretations of MFU as isolating strategy quality, discusses extension to heterogeneous devices and synchronous 1F1B, and proposes environmental benefits without energy measurements. The original BERT topology interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 expands profiling and memory-cost construction details, explicitly discloses the default MIPGap of 1e-4, and documents disabled checkpointing, additional model/hardware settings and HuggingFace compatibility exclusions. The 60-second solver limit and early-stopping rules are retained. The added disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Auto-MAP discussion and Wang et al. (2020) citation, while adding references for LLaMA, Llama 2, activation checkpointing, mixed precision and PaLM/MFU. Its basic positioning against manual, single-category and hierarchical parallelism remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and method undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization. Parallel-strategy explanations move into the background, profiling receives its own section, constraints receive individual explanations, and a worked candidate-solution appendix is added. Terminology changes from strategy searching to optimization, and Jie Li joins the author list.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text, merges and expands the primary results tables, and replaces the numerical ablation table with a bar chart. It adds method-comparison and candidate-solution diagrams and an estimation-error plot, redraws existing explanatory figures, and corrects the scalability plot's optimization-time axis label. The ablation chart no longer supplies exact numerical entries.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central argument by accommodating communication bottlenecks, adding direct Alpa comparisons and testing the previously unvalidated cost estimates. Clearer profiling and constraint explanations also make the method easier to assess. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: the ± quantities remain undefined, Figure 6 shows negative errors despite Equation 9's absolute-error definition, and the appendix inconsistently describes LLaMA precision. Those issues limit confidence in parts of the expanded evidence.
